stem: Alkaline earth metals have valency 2. This means that their position in the modern periodic table is in ____ .
solution: Alkaline earth metals (Be, Mg, Ca ...) have 2 electrons in their outermost shell and valency 2, so they belong to Group 2 of the modern periodic table. Answer: (A) Group 2.

stem: The reaction in which ions in the reactants are exchanged to form a precipitate is called as ____ reaction.
solution: When ions of the reactants are exchanged to form an insoluble precipitate, it is a double displacement (precipitation) reaction, e.g. \(BaCl_2 + Na_2SO_4 \rightarrow BaSO_4\downarrow + 2NaCl\). Answer: (D) Double Displacement.

stem: ____ is used to make a solenoid type coil in an electric bulb.
solution: The filament (solenoid-type coil) of an electric bulb is made of tungsten because tungsten has a very high melting point (about \(3400^\circ C\)) and high resistivity, so it glows white-hot without melting. Answer: (C) Tungsten.

stem: Light changes its direction when going from one transparent medium to another transparent medium. This process is called ____ .
solution: The bending (change of direction) of light as it passes from one transparent medium into another, due to change in its speed, is called refraction. Answer: (D) Refraction.

stem: \(CaO + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2 + Heat\) is an example of ____ reaction.
solution: In \(CaO + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2 + Heat\), heat is released (evolved) along with the product, so it is an exothermic reaction. Answer: (A) Exothermic.

stem: State whether true or false: A redox reaction takes place during cellular respiration.
solution: True. During cellular respiration glucose is oxidised while oxygen is reduced, so oxidation and reduction occur together, i.e. a redox reaction takes place: \(C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O + energy\).

stem: Find the odd one out: Loudspeaker, microphone, electric motor, magnet.
solution: Magnet. Loudspeaker, microphone and electric motor are devices/appliances that work using the magnetic effect of electric current (or electromagnetic induction), whereas a magnet is only a component, not a device.

stem: What is the reason for twinkling of stars?
solution: Twinkling of stars is due to atmospheric refraction of starlight. As starlight passes through layers of air of continuously changing optical density (refractive index) and temperature, it bends by varying amounts, so the apparent position and brightness of the star keep fluctuating, making the star appear to twinkle.

stem:
Match the columns:

| Column 'A' | Column 'B' |
| --- | --- |
| Simple microscope | (a) used to observe minute objects |
|  | (b) used to see distant objects |
|  | (c) used for watch repair |
solution: Simple microscope \(\rightarrow\) (c) used for watch repair. A simple microscope is a single convex lens (magnifying glass) used by watch-makers and jewellers to see small parts enlarged, so it is matched with 'used for watch repair'. (It magnifies minute objects; option (b) 'to see distant objects' is a telescope, not a microscope.)

stem: Name the behaviour of water between its temperature from \(0^\circ C\) to \(4^\circ C\).
solution: It is called the anomalous behaviour (anomalous expansion) of water. Between \(0^\circ C\) and \(4^\circ C\), water contracts on heating (its volume decreases instead of increasing), attaining maximum density at \(4^\circ C\).

stem: Give scientific reason: While going from left to right within a period, the size of atom decreases.
solution: On going from left to right within a period, the atomic number increases by one at each step, so the nuclear charge (number of protons) increases while the new electrons are added to the same outermost shell (the number of shells stays the same). The increased nuclear charge pulls the electrons of the same shell more strongly towards the nucleus, so the atomic radius (size of the atom) decreases across a period.

stem: Give scientific reason: For electric power transmission, copper or aluminium wire is used.
solution: Copper and aluminium are used for electric power transmission because they are excellent conductors of electricity (very low electrical resistivity), they are highly ductile so they can be drawn into long thin wires, and they are relatively cheap and easily available. These properties allow current to be carried over long distances with least loss of energy.

stem: Give scientific reason: In some countries, ethanol is used as an additive to increase the efficiency of petrol.
solution: Ethanol is a clean fuel that burns almost completely. When it is added to petrol, the mixture burns more completely and efficiently, releasing more energy and producing fewer harmful pollutants (such as carbon monoxide and unburnt hydrocarbons). It also raises the octane rating of the fuel and saves petrol, so ethanol is used as an additive to increase the efficiency of petrol.

stem: Name and state the principle used to measure the specific heat capacity of a substance.
solution: The principle of heat exchange (method of mixtures) is used. Principle: when a hot body and a cold body are placed in thermal contact, heat flows from the body at higher temperature to the body at lower temperature until both attain a common (equal) temperature; assuming no heat is lost to the surroundings, the heat energy lost by the hot body is equal to the heat energy gained by the cold body (heat lost = heat gained).

stem: What is done to prevent rusting of iron door of your house?
solution: Rusting is prevented by not allowing the iron surface to come in contact with air and moisture. The iron door is coated with a protective layer, e.g. by painting it, applying grease/oil, galvanising (coating with a layer of zinc) or electroplating. Painting the door is the common everyday method used at home.

stem: Distinguish between mass and weight.
solution:
Distinction between mass and weight:

| Mass | Weight |
| --- | --- |
| It is the amount (quantity) of matter contained in a body. | It is the force with which the earth attracts the body. |
| It is a scalar quantity. | It is a vector quantity. |
| Its SI unit is the kilogram (kg). | Its SI unit is the newton (N). |
| It remains constant everywhere. | It changes from place to place with the value of \(g\). |
| It is measured with a beam balance. | It is measured with a spring balance. |
| Represented as \(m\). | Given by \(W = mg\). |

stem: The 'rocket' is a type of fire cracker used in Diwali. (a) Name the launcher. (b) Name the law on which its working is based.
solution:
(a) The launcher of the fire-cracker 'rocket' is a bottle (a glass or plastic bottle in which the rocket is stood upright before it is lighted).
(b) Its working is based on Newton's third law of motion (the law of action and reaction): the hot gases are thrown out backward/downward and the equal and opposite reaction pushes the rocket forward/upward. This is equivalently explained by the law of conservation of momentum.

stem: What is meant by decomposition reaction? Write the chemical reaction of decomposition of sugar on heating.
solution:
A decomposition reaction is a reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances, usually on being supplied energy in the form of heat, light or electricity.
Decomposition of sugar on heating: \(C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 12C + 11H_2O\). On heating, sugar decomposes into carbon (a black residue) and water vapour.

subtopic: Free Fall and Acceleration due to Gravity
stem: An iron ball of mass 3 kg is released from a height of 125 m and falls freely to the ground. Assuming that the value of \(g\) is \(10\ m/s^2\), calculate: (a) Time taken by the ball to reach the ground. (b) Velocity of the ball on reaching the ground.
solution:
Given: \(h = 125\ m,\ g = 10\ m/s^2,\ u = 0\) (released from rest).
(a) Using \(h = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2:\ 125 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 \Rightarrow 125 = 5t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 25 \Rightarrow t = 5\ s\).
(b) Using \(v = u + gt:\ v = 0 + 10 \times 5 = 50\ m/s\).
So the ball takes 5 s to reach the ground and strikes the ground with a velocity of \(50\ m/s\). (Mass 3 kg is not needed for these calculations.)

stem: Write the name and symbol of the element from the description: (a) The most electronegative atom. (b) The atom having smallest atomic mass. (c) The noble gas with the smallest atomic radius.
solution:
(a) The most electronegative atom: Fluorine (F).
(b) The atom having the smallest atomic mass: Hydrogen (H).
(c) The noble gas with the smallest atomic radius: Helium (He).

stem: (a) What happens when copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid? What is the colour of the gas released during the reaction? (b) Write its balanced chemical equation. (c) Write the names of reactants and products.
solution:
(a) Copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid to form copper nitrate, nitrogen dioxide gas and water. The gas released, nitrogen dioxide \(NO_2\), is reddish-brown in colour.
(b) \(Cu + 4HNO_3(conc.) \rightarrow Cu(NO_3)_2 + 2NO_2\uparrow + 2H_2O\).
(c) Reactants: copper and (concentrated) nitric acid. Products: copper nitrate, nitrogen dioxide and water.

stem: Name the following diagrams and explain the concept behind them: [two diagrams, labelled a and b, each showing a hand with the thumb, forefinger and middle finger held mutually perpendicular with directional arrows].
solution:
The two diagrams show Fleming's hand rules, in which the thumb, forefinger and middle finger are held mutually perpendicular to one another.
(a) Fleming's Left Hand Rule - used for the electric motor. It gives the direction of the force (motion) acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field: the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field, the middle finger in the direction of the current, and the thumb then gives the direction of the force / motion of the conductor.
(b) Fleming's Right Hand Rule - used for the electric generator (dynamo). It gives the direction of the induced current when a conductor is moved in a magnetic field: the forefinger points along the magnetic field, the thumb along the direction of motion of the conductor, and the middle finger then gives the direction of the induced current. (The labels a and b correspond to the two hand diagrams shown; assign by the finger directions in the figure.)
figureNote: Two hand diagrams labelled a. and b., each with three mutually perpendicular arrows (thumb/forefinger/middle finger) illustrating Fleming's Left Hand and Right Hand rules, p-07

stem: Answer the following with respect to the 'Formation of Rainbow': (a) Draw a neat diagram to show the formation of rainbow. (b) Name any two natural processes involved in the formation of rainbow. (c) What does a small droplet of water act as?
solution:
(a) [Diagram to be drawn: sunlight entering a spherical water droplet, undergoing refraction on entering, then total internal reflection at the back of the droplet, and dispersion into the seven colours (VIBGYOR) on emerging out to the observer's eye.]
(b) Any two of the natural processes: refraction of light, dispersion of light, and total internal reflection of light.
(c) A small droplet of water acts as a tiny prism, which refracts and disperses the sunlight into its seven constituent colours.

stem: Name the following: (a) The two metals which can be cut with a knife. (b) A sound is produced when certain metals are struck. Name this property of metals. (c) The non-metallic substance which is a good conductor of electricity.
solution:
(a) The two metals that can be cut with a knife: Sodium (Na) and Potassium (K).
(b) The property by which metals produce a ringing sound when struck is called sonorousness (metals are said to be sonorous).
(c) The non-metal that is a good conductor of electricity: Graphite (an allotrope of carbon).

stem: Answer the following questions with the help of the given diagram [an electrolytic cell: a silver plate as the anode and an aluminium spoon as the cathode dipped in an electrolyte, connected to a cell, with \(Ag^+\) and \(NO_3^-\) ions in the solution]: (a) Name the process shown in the diagram. (b) How does this process take place? (c) Give two examples in which this process is used.
solution:
(a) The process shown is electroplating (electro-deposition) - here, electroplating of silver on an aluminium spoon by passing an electric current (electrolysis).
(b) When electric current is passed, the silver anode gradually dissolves, releasing \(Ag^+\) ions into the electrolyte. These \(Ag^+\) ions move to the cathode (the aluminium spoon), where they gain electrons and get deposited as a thin, uniform layer of silver; the \(NO_3^-\) ions move towards the anode. Thus silver is transferred from the anode and coated on the object at the cathode.
(c) Examples (any two): silver-plating of spoons, ornaments and utensils; gold-plating of jewellery; chromium/nickel-plating of car parts, taps and cycle handlebars to prevent corrosion and improve appearance.
figureNote: Electrolytic cell diagram: 'Cell' at top, silver plate anode (left), aluminium spoon cathode (right), with Ag+ and NO3- ions and electron flow arrows in the electrolyte, p-08

solution:
(a) Type: Navigation satellite; Function: to fix the location of any place on the earth's surface; Indian series: IRNSS (NavIC); Launch vehicle: PSLV.
(b) Weather satellite; Function: to observe and forecast the weather (study clouds, rainfall, storms and cyclones); Indian series: INSAT; Launch vehicle: GSLV.

subtopic: Human Eye and Defects of Vision
stem: (a) Draw a neat labelled diagram of human eye. (b) What is the minimum distance of distinct vision for a normal human eye? (c) Name the capacity of the eye lens to change its focal length as per need. (d) Name the defect of eye vision in which the focussing power of eye lens decreases with age.
solution:
(a) [Neat labelled diagram of the human eye to be drawn, showing: cornea, aqueous humour, iris, pupil, eye lens, ciliary muscles, vitreous humour, retina, optic nerve and blind spot.]
(b) The minimum distance of distinct vision for a normal human eye is 25 cm.
(c) The capacity of the eye lens to change (adjust) its focal length as per need is called the power of accommodation.
(d) The defect in which the focussing power of the eye lens decreases with age (so the near point recedes) is called presbyopia.

stem: Atomic number of chlorine is 17. (a) Write the electronic configuration of chlorine. (b) What is the number of electrons in the valence shell of chlorine? (c) Write the molecular formula of chlorine. (d) Name the type of bond in the formation of chlorine molecule. (e) Draw the electron dot structure of a chlorine molecule.
solution:
Chlorine has atomic number 17.
(a) Electronic configuration: 2, 8, 7.
(b) Number of electrons in the valence (outermost) shell = 7.
(c) Molecular formula of chlorine = \(Cl_2\).
(d) The bond formed is a covalent bond (a single covalent bond formed by mutual sharing of one pair of electrons).
(e) [Electron dot structure to be drawn: two chlorine atoms each with 7 outer electrons share one pair of electrons between them, giving one shared pair (the Cl-Cl bond) plus three lone pairs on each Cl atom, so that each chlorine attains a stable octet of 8 electrons: written as :Cl:Cl: with a shared electron pair between the two Cl atoms.]
